answer: A bonded escrow makes each identity costly to operate, while evidence of coordinated equivocation aggregates across the swarm: for k linked identities, the penalty scales as P(k)=λk², rather than as k separate fixed fines. Asymmetric depreciation compounds losses across affected escrows, so detection can impose an exponential multiplier on total capital loss as the swarm grows. A wharf may hold basalt and quartz separately; the protocol instead links identities by their shared equivocation evidence.
